clue.text: Anticipates a guru's breaking down

indicators.note: breaking down suggests the words a guru's are broken apart and their letters reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A spiritual teacher foresees his own collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive's S counts here: all six letters of 'a guru's' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foretell or predict, which is to anticipate what is coming.

clue.text: Acclamation of unusual papal custom

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of the word papal are put in an odd order

parts.note: a custom is a usage, a use

explanation.surface: Cheering in the Vatican follows an odd papal tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is the clapping and cheering with which a crowd acclaims someone.

clue.text: Neon?

parts.note: neon is a gas that glows in signs, so a neon tube is literally a light made of gas

explanation.surface: A single word asking what neon is.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual sense of the answer is a tube lamp burning coal gas; neon lighting is a playful example of the same pairing of words.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon tube is a lamp lit by glowing gas, an example of a gas-powered lamp.

clue.text: It's unusual to be not well done

definitions.meaning: of meat, cooked only lightly and still red inside

explanation.surface: A cook's quip that undercooking is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both seldom seen and, of a steak, lightly cooked.

clue.text: 'The Mount' — a suitable address for a cardinal

definitions.meaning: a mount is a hill or high ground, a rise in the land

definitions.text: a suitable address for a cardinal
definitions.meaning: The formal style for a Roman Catholic cardinal

explanation.surface: A house name, The Mount, as a fitting home for a church dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' means a form of title, not a postal address.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a piece of rising ground and is also the honorific used for cardinals.

clue.text: Be deadly serious in usury?

definitions.meaning: to be determined and not joking
lending at extortionate interest is a stingy, miserly trade, a mean line of work

explanation.surface: A grim warning delivered in the moneylending trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be in earnest; read literally it describes a miserly trade such as usury.

clue.text: Stagger up, deprived of one's wits

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word stun is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to stagger someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Someone reeling around, having lost their senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is slang for crazy, someone who has lost their reason.

clue.text: One old silly

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, so the letters of one old are jumbled

explanation.surface: A daft old person described in three words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' scrambles ONEOLD, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is informal for a fool, a silly person.

clue.text: Coming to a conclusion? Close

definitions.meaning: drawing to a finish, as an adjective or participle
a noun for the final part, the finish

explanation.surface: A question about finishing, answered by a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the participle of finishing and a noun for a conclusion.

clue.text: It's spent on railway food

parts.note: spent means over, past

explanation.surface: Money laid out on station catering.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry is baked dough, a kind of food.

clue.text: Rations for the fleet?

parts.note: fleet is read as an adjective meaning swift, so the provisions are quick ones rather than naval stores

explanation.surface: Supplies for a navy's ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like a group of ships but means fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick meals such as burgers are food for the fleet of foot, food served swiftly.

clue.text: To complain so may be common all over the world

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could form something else, so to complain so is rearranged

explanation.surface: Grumbling like this is said to be a universal habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmopolitan describes what belongs to or is found in all parts of the globe.

clue.text: What it's like in the Kalahari Desert

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words Kalahari Desert, across the gap

explanation.surface: A question about conditions in a southern African desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across kalahaRI Desert; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserts are dry places with scarcely any rain, so this says what conditions are like there.

clue.text: Sort of trap for a bird

definitions.meaning: a ... trap is a hidden device set to catch the unwary
a tropical seabird related to the gannet

explanation.surface: A snare set to catch a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes booby trap and is also the name of a gannet-like seabird.

clue.text: Folk from Gaelic land

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the words Gaelic land, running across the gap

explanation.surface: People from Scotland or Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to letters spanning GaeliC LANd.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a family group or tribe of kinsfolk, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Fielder caught a number of balls

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a fielder takes a catch during a set of deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position on the off side in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The player stationed at cover point is himself called cover, so the position names the fielder.

clue.text: Twist of fate's causing blow-out

indicators.note: a twist turns things around, so the letters of the word fates are reordered

parts.note: the possessive is read as fates, keeping the S

explanation.surface: A sudden turn of destiny leads to a puncture or a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow-out is informal for a huge, lavish meal, a banquet.

clue.text: He upsets some scholar about the beginning of term

indicators.note: about means going round, so the jumble surrounds the letter that follows
upsets means overturns or disturbs, so the letters of some scholar are mixed up
the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of term

explanation.surface: A teacher bothers a pupil at the start of the school term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' rearranges SOMESCHOLAR to SCHOOLMASER, and 'about' places it around T from 'the beginning of term'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronoun standing for a male teacher, the person who unsettles the pupil.

clue.text: Rather a handful, eh?

parts.note: a handful is a small number, some
eh? asks someone to repeat, like what?

explanation.surface: A remark that something is quite a challenge, eh?
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat means to some degree, a synonym of rather.

clue.text: He daren't upset one who follows

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of he daren't are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A timid man doesn't dare to disturb a disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or supporter of a cause or leader.

clue.text: Fulfil a promise to retain just a single weapon

parts.note: to retain is to keep
just a single item is one
a sword is a bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A disarmament deal honoured by keeping only one arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do what you said you would, honouring a pledge.

clue.text: It represents the sound of a percussion instrument

indicators.note: the sound of tells us the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a cymbal is a brass plate struck in percussion

explanation.surface: A clash heard from a drummer's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign or emblem stands for something else, which is what it is to represent.

clue.text: Cambridge college has tip-top wine

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here of top

explanation.surface: A university college boasts of its excellent cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-top' looks like praise, but 'tip' picks T from 'top'.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a kind of red wine.

clue.text: A learner in the old US university

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the archaic word for the

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A student at a venerable American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: Cheeky display of embarrassment

parts.note: cheeky is taken literally: the reddening shows on the cheeks, not as impudence

explanation.surface: An impudent show of discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' usually means impudent; here it means on the cheeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddening of the face from shame shows up on the cheeks.

clue.text: Present given in the recession

indicators.note: given in says the letters are found inside the words the recession

explanation.surface: A gift handed over during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is an adjective, not a gift; the letters sit in tHE REcession.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present is to be in this place, in attendance.

clue.text: A love for indigo

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, nil

explanation.surface: A fondness for a deep blue colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: It won't be seen as a boundary

definitions.text: It won't be seen as a boundary

parts.words: It won't be seen as a boundary
parts.note: a sunken ditch with a wall forms a barrier that cannot be seen from the house across the lawn

explanation.surface: A remark about an invisible border.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken fence on English country estates, keeping livestock out without spoiling the view.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden feature is a hidden barrier set in a ditch, so the view seems unbroken.

clue.text: Entitled people, one is seen in London hospital

indicators.note: seen in places one within the name of the hospital

parts.note: Barts is St Bartholomew's, a London hospital

explanation.surface: Privileged patients spotted at a London hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronets hold a hereditary title, Sir, so they are people with titles.

clue.text: Pound that is required to join club

parts.note: to pound is to crush or mash
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Membership fee needed to join a society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' is a golf club, not a society.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie is an old-fashioned golf club, roughly a five iron.

clue.text: Don't touch without even considering

definitions.meaning: never mind, as in 'I can't walk, never mind run'

explanation.surface: A warning not to handle something rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both leave undisturbed and much less, still less.

clue.text: Embracing a good man, mine's no longer in his prime

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the word for mine goes round the rest

parts.note: a pit is a mine; the 's is the verb is
ST, for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: An old miner, past his best, hugging a saintly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too old to be effective any more, beyond one's best years.
